subjects.displayTitle: Transcendence and the unknowability of God
subjects.introduction: To say that God cannot be known sounds at first like a closed door, yet Bahá’u’lláh treats it as the beginning of every real approach to the divine. The Essence of God, He teaches, is beyond number and direction, beyond rising and setting, beyond the farthest flight of the heart; whatever a mind manages to picture is a creature of that mind and not its Creator. The journey begins by admitting this, and then discovering how much remains open: the signs scattered through creation, the names and attributes by which God permits Himself to be praised, and the Manifestation, the mirror in which the sun appears without descending into it. The question deepens as it travels. A mineral cannot conceive of sight, so how far can the lower reach toward the higher? What can language carry before it meets its limit? And when praise itself confesses that it falls short, why does the longing to pray only grow stronger? Humility before an unsearchable God turns out to be a form of nearness, and a reason for service.

order.why: Begin with the distinction between the divine Essence and everything a created mind can describe. Oneness here is not simply the first item in a numerical series; nor do spatial height, direction, outwardness or inwardness confine God. The texts also permit remembrance and praise through divine generosity. The account of differing spiritual perspectives leads through successive understandings, including warnings against mistaking an attained station for the end of the journey. Read its qualifications and poems together. Explore the actual neighbors on transcendence and immanence, divine independence, and the lower being unable to comprehend the higher. shortened: And the movement which is coming into existence of the world is a movement of Love. This is clearly indicated by the Apostle when he says (conveying God's own words): 'I was a hidden treasure, and I loved to be known.' If it were not for this love, the world would never have appeared in this concrete existence. In this sense, the movement of the world toward existence was a movement of Love which brought it into existence.
